2026-09-09T12:39:20.1955953Z <mcp-clis>
2026-09-09T12:39:20.1956480Z ## MCP Servers Mounted as Shell CLI Commands
2026-09-09T12:39:20.1956895Z 
2026-09-09T12:39:20.1957259Z The following servers are available as CLI commands on `PATH`:
2026-09-09T12:39:20.1957793Z 
2026-09-09T12:39:20.1958278Z - `safeoutputs` — run `safeoutputs --help` to see available tools
2026-09-09T12:39:20.1958818Z 
2026-09-09T12:39:20.1960524Z > **IMPORTANT**: For `safeoutputs` and `mcpscripts`, **always use the CLI commands** listed above instead of the equivalent MCP tools. The CLI wrappers are the preferred interface — do **not** call their MCP tools directly even though they may appear in your tool list.
2026-09-09T12:39:20.1962421Z >
2026-09-09T12:39:20.1968238Z > For `safeoutputs`, treat every successful command as a real write-intent declaration. Do **not** use `safeoutputs` for exploratory probing, auth checks, placeholder payloads, repeated "try again" variants, or manual runtime experiments. When you need a safe-output, emit the final intended call once. If you are not ready to perform the real action, use `noop` or `report_incomplete` instead.
2026-09-09T12:39:20.1971112Z >
2026-09-09T12:39:20.1972032Z > For all other servers listed here, they are **only** available as CLI commands and are **not** available as MCP tools.
2026-09-09T12:39:20.1972872Z 
2026-09-09T12:39:20.1973074Z ### How to Use
2026-09-09T12:39:20.1973347Z 
2026-09-09T12:39:20.1974203Z Each server is a standalone executable on your `PATH`. Invoke it from bash like any other shell command:
2026-09-09T12:39:20.1975265Z 
2026-09-09T12:39:20.1975491Z ```bash
2026-09-09T12:39:20.1976156Z # Call a tool — pass arguments as --name value pairs
2026-09-09T12:39:20.1976982Z <server-name> <tool-name> --param1 value1 --param2 value2
2026-09-09T12:39:20.1977668Z ```
2026-09-09T12:39:20.1977909Z 
2026-09-09T12:39:20.1978211Z **Example** — using the `playwright` CLI:
2026-09-09T12:39:20.1978807Z ```bash
2026-09-09T12:39:20.1979408Z playwright --help                                  # list all browser tools
2026-09-09T12:39:20.1980272Z playwright browser_navigate --url https://example.com
2026-09-09T12:39:20.1981196Z playwright browser_snapshot                        # capture page accessibility tree
2026-09-09T12:39:20.1982008Z ```
2026-09-09T12:39:20.1982243Z 
2026-09-09T12:39:20.1982938Z **Example** — using the `safeoutputs` CLI (safe outputs) when you are ready to emit the final real action:
2026-09-09T12:39:20.1983882Z ```bash
2026-09-09T12:39:20.1984509Z safeoutputs add_comment --issue_number 42 --body "Analysis complete"
2026-09-09T12:39:20.1989725Z ```
2026-09-09T12:39:20.1990013Z 
2026-09-09T12:39:20.1990462Z **Example** — using the `mcpscripts` CLI (mcp-scripts):
2026-09-09T12:39:20.1991372Z ```bash
2026-09-09T12:39:20.1991983Z mcpscripts --help                                  # list all script tools
2026-09-09T12:39:20.1992932Z mcpscripts mcpscripts-gh --args "pr list --repo owner/repo --limit 5"
2026-09-09T12:39:20.1993696Z ```
2026-09-09T12:39:20.1993928Z 
2026-09-09T12:39:20.1994220Z ### Passing Multiple or Complex Arguments (Preferred)
2026-09-09T12:39:20.1994697Z 
2026-09-09T12:39:20.1996725Z **Preferred approach for any tool call with multiple or complex arguments**: supply a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel. The bridge parses stdin as the argument object, preserving all native types (numbers, booleans, arrays) without shell-quoting issues.
2026-09-09T12:39:20.1998459Z 
2026-09-09T12:39:20.1998673Z ```bash
2026-09-09T12:39:20.1999185Z # Full argument payload as JSON via printf pipe
2026-09-09T12:39:20.2000126Z printf '{"issue_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody paragraph one.\n\nBody paragraph two."}' \
2026-09-09T12:39:20.2001010Z   | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-09-09T12:39:20.2001366Z 
2026-09-09T12:39:20.2001919Z # Works with any tool — just match the parameter names from <server> <tool> --help
2026-09-09T12:39:20.2003031Z printf '{"title":"Fix: something","body":"Details here","labels":["bug","priority-high"]}' \
2026-09-09T12:39:20.2003917Z   | safeoutputs create_issue .
2026-09-09T12:39:20.2004450Z ```
2026-09-09T12:39:20.2004684Z 
2026-09-09T12:39:20.2019804Z **When pipes are blocked by the bash security policy**, write the payload to a file first and use **file redirection** with the `.` sentinel instead:
2026-09-09T12:39:20.2020963Z 
2026-09-09T12:39:20.2021185Z ```bash
2026-09-09T12:39:20.2022079Z # Step 1 — write the JSON payload to a file using the Write tool or a bash heredoc
2026-09-09T12:39:20.2023108Z # Step 2 — redirect the file into the CLI command using '<'
2026-09-09T12:39:20.2023940Z safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-09-09T12:39:20.2024445Z 
2026-09-09T12:39:20.2025578Z # This is equivalent to piping but does not require a separate command before '|'
2026-09-09T12:39:20.2026555Z safeoutputs add_comment . < /tmp/comment.json
2026-09-09T12:39:20.2027179Z ```
2026-09-09T12:39:20.2027414Z 
2026-09-09T12:39:20.2027660Z > **Why prefer JSON payload mode?**
2026-09-09T12:39:20.2028593Z > - Single operation for any number of arguments — no repeated `--key value` flags
2026-09-09T12:39:20.2029741Z > - Native types (integers, booleans, arrays) are preserved exactly as specified
2026-09-09T12:39:20.2030856Z > - No shell quoting or escaping needed for newlines, quotes, or special characters
2026-09-09T12:39:20.2032004Z > - Agents can construct the payload as a structured object before emitting the command
2026-09-09T12:39:20.2033288Z > - File redirection (`< file`) works even when pipes (`|`) are restricted
2026-09-09T12:39:20.2033894Z 
2026-09-09T12:39:20.2034103Z ### Notes
2026-09-09T12:39:20.2034343Z 
2026-09-09T12:39:20.2035373Z - **Prefer JSON payload mode** (`. < file` or `printf '{...}' | server tool .`) for any call with multiple arguments or complex values
2026-09-09T12:39:20.2037048Z - All parameters can also be passed as `--name value` pairs; boolean flags can be set with `--flag` (no value) to mean `true`
2026-09-09T12:39:20.2038528Z - Use `.` as the only argument to parse stdin as a JSON object (all parameters supplied at once)
2026-09-09T12:39:20.2040023Z - Parameter names with hyphens or underscores are interchangeable (e.g. `issue-number` and `issue_number` both work)
2026-09-09T12:39:20.2041413Z - Output is printed to stdout; errors are printed to stderr with a non-zero exit code
2026-09-09T12:39:20.2042701Z - Run the CLI commands inside a `bash` tool call — they are shell executables, not MCP tools
2026-09-09T12:39:20.2043812Z - These CLI commands are read-only and cannot be modified by the agent
2026-09-09T12:39:20.2044591Z </mcp-clis>
